records.name: Center City Mosque
records.summary: A small mosque on Walnut Street that holds daily prayers, Friday prayers and weekly Quran circles for children, youth and adults. It also holds Ramadan iftar gatherings and Eid prayers.
records.what_you_do: Come to the second Friday prayer, which is open to brothers and sisters, or ask about the Quran circles. Special programs include Ramadan iftar gatherings, Eid prayers and community service projects.

schedule.text: Friday prayer: first session 1:10 to 1:35 pm for brothers only, second session 1:50 to 2:15 pm for brothers and sisters. Daily prayer times are on the home page. Quran circles meet weekly but have no posted time.

cost.text: No fee is listed. Donations help the mosque expand its space.

first_step.how: Come to the 1:50 pm Friday prayer, which is open to men and women, or call 267-817-4433 or email centercitymosque@gmail.com to ask about classes.
first_step.basis: The contact page invites visitors to come for prayer, ask a question or join the community, and gives a phone number and email. The Friday page has arrival tips, but there is no formal orientation.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each Friday session lasts about 25 minutes and includes a short talk (khutbah) followed by the prayer. The page asks visitors to arrive 10 to 15 minutes early, find a quiet place and listen to the talk quietly.
first_visit_tips: Arrive 10 to 15 minutes early to find a quiet spot.
Silence your phone and dress modestly.
Parking nearby is limited, so allow extra time.
The 1:10 pm session is for men only, so women and families should come to the 1:50 pm session.

records.notes: The Friday page lists two Friday sessions, but the site header also lists a third Jumu'ah at 1:50 pm, so confirm the sessions with the mosque before a first visit. Quran class times are not posted; the Quran and contact pages both ask people to call or email. The home page says Friday prayer is streamed live on YouTube; that is watch only, so online_ok is not set. Dress code, shoes, entrance, transit and wheelchair access are not stated on the pages read.

records.name: Center for Hope
records.summary: A shelter and support program for adults experiencing homelessness in Philadelphia. It offers emergency housing, case management, job and life-skills training, and medical and mental health help.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer through the Get Involved form on the group's site, or donate through its PayPal link. Shelter stays are for people referred through the City's homeless services office.

first_step.how: Fill in the Get Involved form on cfhphila.org to start volunteering. The site does not say what happens after that.
first_step.basis: A public form is a clear way in, but the site does not describe volunteer steps, training, minimum age or time commitment.

records.notes: The October items (Hope Drive, Hoops4Hope games, Hope Shop opening) print no year on the site, so they are not used as dated evidence and have been removed from the schedule. No volunteer page was found: cfhphila.org/get-involved returned 404, and the contact and programs pages describe no volunteer steps. The programs page does not list transitional housing, so the summary no longer mentions it. Walk-in access and office hours are not stated. One early guess at a centerforhope.org address redirected to another organization's domain; it was not followed or used.

records.name: Central Philadelphia Friends Meeting
records.summary: A Quaker meeting that worships on Sunday mornings in the meetinghouse at Friends Center in Center City, in person or on Zoom. It offers childcare for young children and religious education for school-age children.
records.what_you_do: Join Sunday worship at 11 am, stay for the social time afterward, or ask the office about children's religious education and childcare. The site also lists committees on peace and social concerns, pastoral care, and community life.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 11 am at 1501 Cherry Street or on Zoom, about an hour long. The site lists childcare for children up to age 4 and religious education for ages 5 to 12, but its dates are mixed, so confirm with the office.

cost.text: No admission cost is listed. The meeting invites gifts through an online donation page.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 11 am at 1501 Cherry Street, or join on Zoom by asking the office for the link.
first_step.basis: The site has a page written for visitors, invites newcomers to worship and community life whether or not they are members, and says how to start: come on a Sunday or join by Zoom.
first_step.what_to_expect: Worship lasts about an hour and is held in silence, with no planned hymns or sermon. Anyone may stand to speak if moved to, and visitors are not asked to. Afterward there is a social time with refreshments.
first_visit_tips: Plan on about an hour for worship, then stay for refreshments and conversation.
Zoom is an option if you would rather join from home; ask the office for the link.
Call 215-241-7260 or email office@cpmm.org about parking, entrances or accessibility, which the site does not cover.
Ask the office about children's classes before you bring children, since the site's dates are mixed.

records.notes: The Families and Children page could not be fetched in full. Its childcare and First Day School details come from a search summary, which said those pages look about 2.5 to 3 years old and that dates may have changed, so the record asks visitors to confirm with the office. The Welcome page does not cover greeters, dress, arrival time, entrance, accessibility, parking or transit. The Getting to Us page returned 404. The Zoom login details sit on the worship page and are not recorded here. The events page is archived and shows no current dated events. Friends Center's own site lists Sunday hours inconsistently, so check before visiting the building.

records.name: Madre Tierra Philly
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that makes Spanish-language radio, TV and online programs about gender equality and violence against Latinas. Its Centro also runs workshops, group talks and women's circles, and lists remote counseling.
records.what_you_do: Watch or listen to its Spanish-language programs, follow its news and social channels, or use the contact form to ask about a project or about becoming an ally. Its Centro page mentions workshops, courses and women's circles, but gives no dates or sign-up steps.

locations.label: Philadelphia (no street address published on its site)

first_step.how: Sign up for news on madretierraphilly.com, or use the contact form there to ask about its workshops, women's circles or becoming an ally.
first_step.basis: The site has a news sign-up and contact forms, but no volunteer, class or event steps with dates. Workshops and women's circles are named without dates or sign-up, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: Kept as publish, but this is mainly a media company. Its public ways in are a news sign-up, contact forms, and the Centro's workshops and women's circles, which have no dates posted, so the owner may want to check that a media producer belongs in the directory. The Centro page also lists madretierraphilly@gmail.com; only the info address is recorded. No street address is published. The blog and events lists show no dated items with a year. The site is mainly in Spanish.

records.name: Chabad House at the University of Pennsylvania (Chabad at Penn)
records.summary: The Chabad house for the University of Pennsylvania on Spruce Street. It offers Shabbat dinners, holiday gatherings and learning for students, has pages for graduate students and alumni, and posts weekly candle lighting times.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for the Chabad Bot by text for event updates, join the mailing list or the Students Weekly Newsletter, or RSVP for a general event, Family Weekend or the High Holidays. Contact the house through its contact page.

schedule.text: Shabbat candle lighting and end times are posted each week on the home page. No regular service or class times are printed.

cost.text: No fees are listed on the house site. It has a donate link.

first_step.how: Sign up for the Chabad Bot by text, then RSVP for the event you want.
first_step.basis: The house offers sign-up and RSVP routes for events, but the pages read do not say newcomers or first-timers are welcome. A testimonial about feeling at home as a new arrival is the closest thing to a welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a first visit in detail. Its main programs for students are Shabbat dinners, holiday events and learning, and the pages read list no fees.
first_visit_tips: RSVP for an event before you come, since the site runs its events through RSVP pages.
The site does not list walk-in times or office hours, so ask through the contact page first.

records.notes: The house's sub-pages (Shabbat Dinner, Learning, RSVP) are hosted on the chabad.org network. The Shabbat Dinner page redirected to chabad.org and was not followed; the /students page on chabadatpenn.com returned 404. Candle lighting times on the home page print no year, so they are not used as dated evidence. The weekly Torah portion date (10/8/2026) appears only inside a link address, not as visible text, so it is not used either. The pages read do not say newcomers are welcome, and no weekly day and time is printed for any program.

records.name: Change Up Sports
records.summary: A free softball and baseball group that runs clinics, camps, leagues and training for young people and adults. Its Philadelphia programs run through rec centers and community groups, and it also runs programs in Sierra Leone and Belize.
records.what_you_do: Players can join free youth and adult clinics, camps and leagues, including an entry-level program with local partners. Coaches, community members and youth workers can take free CPR, first aid and lifesaving training. Supporters can donate equipment, host a drive or join a service trip abroad.

schedule.text: Youth clinics for ages 6 to 18 run in two eight-week sessions each spring and fall at a Cobbs Creek resource center with Community of Compassion CDC.

locations.label: Cobbs Creek resource center (Community of Compassion CDC)

cost.text: Free. The group says it never charges participants for its programs.

first_step.how: Use the contact form on the group's site to ask about the next local clinic, camp or league, and ask which site and time it runs.
first_step.basis: Programs are free and open to kids of all skill levels, but the site does not say how to register for a clinic, camp or league, and its email addresses differ from page to page.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not say how long a clinic runs or who leads it. Some programs also provide snacks, drinks and school supplies.
first_visit_tips: Ask which rec center and what time the next clinic is, since the site does not list dates.

records.notes: Email addresses conflict across the group's pages: kelly@letschangeupsports.org appears on some pages, kelly@changeupsports.org in the footer and on one page, and a misspelled variant on the Get Involved page. One page prints a phone number that another page does not. No email or phone is recorded, so confirm the current contact before publishing. The Philadelphia page lists Mill Creek Recreation Center as a past site, so it is left out of locations. The newest dated item is 2025 program results with no month, so last_sign_of_life is not set. The Get Involved and what-we-do pages list no Philadelphia clinic dates.

records.name: Chester Avenue Community Garden
records.summary: A shared neighborhood garden on Chester Avenue, run by its gardeners. Gardeners work together on monthly work days and on volunteer teams for compost, herbs, mowing, orchard, flowers and more. Neighbors can email the garden to ask about joining.
records.what_you_do: Come to the monthly work day, usually a Saturday morning, to help with tasks that benefit the whole garden. The site also lists volunteer teams with named members, such as compost, herbs, lawn mowing, orchard and CSA pickups.

schedule.text: Work days on the third Saturday of each month, about 9 am to noon, or 8 am to 11 am when it is very hot.

first_step.how: Come to a work day on the third Saturday of the month, and email chester.ave.garden@gmail.com to ask about joining.
first_step.basis: Work days are posted with set times, but the site only invites gardeners to come help. It does not say whether non-gardeners can join a work day or how to become a gardener.
first_step.what_to_expect: A work day runs about three hours in the morning. Teams work on shared tasks such as compost, herbs, mowing, shoveling and pest care, and the site asks gardeners to help with tasks that serve the whole garden.
first_visit_tips: Check the site's 2026 work day list for the coordinator who leads that month.
On very hot days the work day starts at 8 am and ends at 11 am.
Hours are logged in a shared Google Sheet linked from the volunteer hours page.

records.notes: The home page lists a 2026 work day schedule from June to November, with the October 17 work day next, and an empty Upcoming events heading. Status is set to active on the strength of that dated 2026 schedule. Membership, plot waitlist, dues, visitor rules and open days are not on the site. The Instagram link points to an archived account from March 2025, so it is not used as evidence. The email comes from tier 1 sources and does not appear on the garden pages read in this pass. The About page returned 404. The Garden Map and Compost pages linked from the menu were not read.

leads_only.name: Community of Compassion CDC
leads_only.note: Named on Change Up Sports' Philadelphia page as the partner running Cobbs Creek youth clinics. Its own site was not found in this pass.

leads_only.name: Congreso de Latinos Unidos
leads_only.note: Named on Change Up Sports' Philadelphia page as a partner running clinics at Julia de Burgos Elementary. Its own site was not checked.

leads_only.name: Friends Center Corporation
leads_only.note: Named on the Central Philadelphia Friends Meeting site as the building host at 1501 Cherry Street. It is probably a building owner, not a group, so check before any research.

notes: All 7 groups were deep-read on their own sites. Fetch count is 38. Per group, own-site fetches stayed at 6 or fewer; the Friends group also made one fetch of Friends Center Corporation's page (a different organization), used only to confirm the address and a Sunday hours note. One WebSearch was used, for the Friends Meeting families page; its result was a search summary, not a full read, and the record says so. No 403s, bot checks or rate limits were seen. Several guessed URLs returned 404 and were not retried. Verdicts: 7 publish, 0 hide, 0 not_a_group. Owner attention: Madre Tierra is mainly a media company (see its notes); Change Up Sports lists conflicting email addresses, so none is recorded; the Friends Meeting children's dates are mixed, so visitors are told to confirm; the mosque's Friday session count differs between two places on its site. One accidental call to a session widget tool (read_widget_context) happened early in the run. It was read-only, returned nothing and changed nothing.
